text:
The cost of modern medicine is rising, and people disagree about who should pay for it: individuals themselves, or society through the government. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of individual payment argue that people should take responsibility for the cost of their own care. When patients pay something, even a small fee, they tend to use services more carefully, which reduces waste and unnecessary visits. Individual payment can also keep taxes lower and allows people to choose the level of cover that suits them. Competition between private providers may improve quality and shorten waiting times, since clinics must attract patients. A small charge for a routine consultation, for example, may discourage people from seeing a doctor for minor complaints that could be treated at home, leaving more time for those who are seriously ill.

On the other hand, advocates of public funding point out that illness is unpredictable and expensive, so the cost of care should be shared. A serious illness can ruin a family's finances through no fault of its own, and people who delay treatment because they cannot pay often need costlier emergency care later. Public funding protects the poor, keeps the workforce healthy and treats health as a basic right rather than a luxury. A patient who cannot afford cancer treatment, for instance, may lose both health and savings. Shared funding spreads the risk across the whole population, so that no one is left without help.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that society should fund essential care, with modest personal contributions for non-urgent services, because this protects the vulnerable while limiting waste.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: cá nhân hay xã hội chi trả chi phí y tế

plan.think: Mở bài nêu bối cảnh (chi phí y học tăng) rồi hai phe: cá nhân tự trả / xã hội trả qua chính phủ.

Bệnh nhân trả phí thì dùng dịch vụ cẩn thận hơn, giảm lãng phí; thuế thấp hơn; cạnh tranh giữa nhà cung cấp tư nâng chất lượng và giảm thời gian chờ. Ví dụ khoản phí nhỏ cho khám thường quy ngăn người đến bác sĩ vì bệnh vặt.

Bệnh khó đoán và tốn kém; bệnh nặng có thể phá sản gia đình; trì hoãn điều trị vì không đủ tiền thì sau đó cần cấp cứu đắt hơn; sức khoẻ là quyền cơ bản. Ví dụ bệnh nhân ung thư không đủ tiền điều trị.
Xã hội chi trả chăm sóc thiết yếu, cá nhân đóng góp khiêm tốn cho dịch vụ không khẩn cấp để bảo vệ người yếu thế mà vẫn hạn chế lãng phí.
